exact_replacements.before: $A$ is the centralizer algebra $\{X:Xe=eX\}$; in a Jordan-string basis it is a direct product of matrix algebras indexed by the equal string lengths, and it is generated as a vector space by the powers $e^0,\dots,e^{l-1}$ on each string.
exact_replacements.after: $A=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[e]}(V)=\{X:Xe=eX\}$ is the full associative centralizer algebra, with multiplication given by composition. For a Jordan-string decomposition $V=\bigoplus_\alpha R_\alpha$, $R_\alpha=\mathbb C[t]/(t^{p_\alpha})$ with $t$ acting as $e$, its $(\alpha,\beta)$ block is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C[t]}(R_\beta,R_\alpha)$, of dimension $\min(p_\alpha,p_\beta)$: a homomorphism is determined by the image of $1$, which must be killed by $t^{p_\beta}$. Thus all off-diagonal string-homomorphism blocks, including those between unequal lengths, are retained. The algebra need not be semisimple: for a single string of length $2$ it is $\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)$, with nonzero radical $(t)$.

exact_replacements.before: Conversely every element of $\psi(B)$ commutes with the individual $e$-operators and with the place permutations, hence with the diagonal $A$-action.
exact_replacements.after: Conversely every element of $\psi(B)$ commutes with the diagonal $A$-action: for $a\in A$ put $\Delta_d(a)=\sum_{k=1}^d a^{(k)}$; each individual $e^{(j)}$ satisfies $[\Delta_d(a),e^{(j)}]=[a,e]^{(j)}=0$, and each place permutation $P_\sigma$ satisfies $P_\sigma\Delta_d(a)P_\sigma^{-1}=\Delta_d(a)$. These operators generate $\psi(B)$, so their products and linear combinations also commute with every $\Delta_d(a)$.
